planting.note: Plant dormant bare-root canes in late winter to early spring along a support wire.

directions: Glen Doll is a late-season, spine-free floricane raspberry bred by the James Hutton Institute in Scotland, cropping roughly a week after Glen Ample and continuing into mid-August. Plant dormant canes in late winter to early spring along a support wire, since the upright, low-to-moderate vigor canes carry long fruiting laterals well suited to machine or hand harvest. The firm, globular, bright red berries have excellent flavor and freeze well, and the plant carries built-in resistance to the main aphid species that spreads raspberry viruses. Cut spent floricanes to the ground after harvest and tie in the new primocanes for next season's crop.
sources: James Hutton Institute Fruit Breeding Programme variety database

planting.note: Plant dormant bare-root canes in late winter to early spring and train to a trellis.

directions: Glen Eden is an early-to-mid-season floricane raspberry from the James Hutton Institute, bred as improved progeny of Glen Ample and cropping roughly ten to fourteen days ahead of its parent. Plant dormant canes in late winter or early spring and train them to a trellis, since the vigorous canes carry very large, slightly elongated, medium-red berries with balanced sweetness and good disease tolerance. Yields are heavy and consistent, with potential for a modest second flush under mild autumn conditions. Remove fruited canes after harvest and tie in replacement canes to keep the row open and productive.
sources: James Hutton Institute Fruit Breeding Programme variety database

planting.note: Plant dormant bare-root canes in late winter to early spring on a support trellis.

directions: Glen Lyon is an early-to-mid-season floricane raspberry from the James Hutton Institute breeding program that has become a leading commercial variety in parts of southern Europe. Plant dormant canes in late winter to early spring and support them on a trellis, since the canes produce moderately sized, slightly conical berries that ripen to a bright orange-red with a firm texture and a tangy, classic raspberry flavor. The fruit's good shelf life and bright color suit it to fresh-market sale as well as home use. Prune out spent floricanes after harvest and thin new canes to maintain airflow and berry size.
sources: James Hutton Institute Fruit Breeding Programme variety database

planting.note: Plant dormant bare-root canes in late winter to early spring, spacing generously for airflow.

directions: Glen Magna is a late-season floricane raspberry bred by the James Hutton Institute from a cross of Meeker with an SCRI selection line, producing large, fleshy, conical berries in a mid-to-dark red that ripen with a sweet, aromatic flavor. Plant dormant canes in late winter to early spring on a support trellis; the canes suit garden and local-market growing rather than large-scale mechanical harvest. Prune out spent floricanes immediately after harvest and tie in new canes to keep the row productive the following year. Space plants generously to allow good air movement, since dense plantings in humid climates raise disease pressure on late-season fruit.
sources: James Hutton Institute Fruit Breeding Programme variety database

planting.note: Plant canes in spring; new primocanes will bear fruit the same season.

directions: Skye is a mid-to-late-season primocane raspberry from the James Hutton Institute breeding program, selected for very large, firm berries that hold their mid-to-light red color well after picking. Plant canes or dormant primocane stock in spring; the tall, vigorous canes have short internodes and an unusually high number of fruiting laterals, giving strong yields through late summer into fall. The berries are notably sweet and low in acidity, with a mellow flavor that sets the variety apart from tarter, high-acid raspberries. Cut all canes to the ground in late winter, since fruit is borne on the current season's growth.
sources: James Hutton Institute Fruit Breeding Programme variety database

planting.note: Plant canes in spring for an early-starting autumn primocane crop.

directions: Lewis is an early-fruiting primocane raspberry from the James Hutton Institute breeding program, bred to begin its autumn crop earlier than most primocane types. Plant canes in spring; the stout, moderately vigorous canes are easy to manage and carry some of the largest berries among primocane raspberries, with good flavor and shelf life for fresh-market sale. Its notably low chilling requirement makes it a useful option for mild-winter regions where many primocane types fruit too late to finish before frost. Mow or cut all canes to the ground in late winter to reset growth for the next season's primocane crop.
sources: James Hutton Institute Fruit Breeding Programme variety database
